title: The Maze Bell
hook: The corn maze had one rule after dark: if someone calls for help from inside, don't go in.
lines: Every October, I ran the corn maze at the Marsh farm, out past the edge of town.
Old Mr. Marsh gave me one rule on my first night.
After the lights go off, if someone calls for help from inside the maze... don't go in.
Ring the bell by the gate. And let them find their own way out.
All season, the maze was empty by ten. My count always matched.
Then, on the last night, a couple came running out of the corn. Their little girl was gone.
Yellow raincoat. Six years old. The mother couldn't stop shaking.
And deep in the rows... a tiny voice. Help me... I'm lost.
I rang the bell. Again. And again.
The voice stopped. The wind stopped. Even the corn went still.
Please, the mother whispered. Just go get her.
So I grabbed my flashlight... and checked my ticket log one last time.
That couple came in at eight. Two tickets. No child.
And when I looked up... they were standing at the gate, smiling. Waiting for me to go in.
